```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

This script prepares Ostreobium ASVs for phylogenetic placement. It subsets the
full phyloseq object to *Ostreobium* taxa from healthy coral samples, writes the ASV
names to `../data/ostreobium_asvs_healthy.txt` for downstream use, and exports an
ASV–metadata table to
`../../microbiome/data/ASV_table_ostreobium_healthy_present.xlsx`.

The bash chunks (`eval=FALSE`) document the HPC pipeline run on a compute cluster:
reference sequence clustering and alignment (vsearch, mafft, trimal), model
selection (ModelTest-NG), backbone SSU rRNA tree inference (RAxML), and evolutionary
placement of amplicon ASVs onto the backbone using HMMER alignment and RAxML EPA.

Additional R chunks summarise ASV counts per geographic location and coral type, and
check for Ostreobium presence in octocorals.

See `ostreobium_tree_itol.Rmd` for the iTOL annotation step.

```{r load-data}
ps_plas_V3_V4 <- readRDS("../../microbiome/data/ps_final.rds")
```

# Extract Ostreobium ASVs

We extracted 3422 sequences from the dataset.

```{r extract-ostreobium}
library(phyloseq)
library(magrittr)

# 1. Subset to Ostreobium only
ps_ost <- subset_taxa(ps_plas_V3_V4, Genus == "Ostreobium")

# 2. Subset to healthy samples
ps_ost_healthy <- subset_samples(ps_ost, coral_health == "healthy")

# 3. Keep only ASVs present (non-zero) in healthy samples
ps_ost_healthy_present <- prune_taxa(
  taxa_sums(ps_ost_healthy) > 0,
  ps_ost_healthy
)

# 4. Extract ASV names and write to file
ostreobium_asvs_healthy <- taxa_names(ps_ost_healthy_present)

dir.create("../data", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
write(ostreobium_asvs_healthy, file = "../data/ostreobium_asvs_healthy.txt")  # phylogenies/data/
```

```{r sanity-checks}
length(taxa_names(ps_ost))             # ASVs before filtering
length(ostreobium_asvs_healthy)        # ASVs after healthy + presence filtering
all(taxa_sums(ps_ost_healthy_present) > 0)  # confirm no zero-abundance taxa remain
```

# With metadata

```{r export-metadata}
library(phyloseq)
library(tidyverse)
library(openxlsx)

# 1. Convert OTU table to a data frame (samples as rows)
otu_df <- as.data.frame(otu_table(ps_ost_healthy_present))
if (taxa_are_rows(ps_ost_healthy_present)) otu_df <- t(otu_df)
otu_df <- as.data.frame(otu_df)
otu_df$SampleID <- rownames(otu_df)

# 2. Pivot long and join sample metadata
sample_df <- as.data.frame(sample_data(ps_ost_healthy_present))
sample_df$SampleID <- rownames(sample_df)

otu_long <- otu_df %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -SampleID, names_to = "ASV", values_to = "Abundance") %>%
  left_join(sample_df, by = "SampleID")

# 3. Join taxonomy
tax_df <- as.data.frame(tax_table(ps_ost_healthy_present))
tax_df$ASV <- rownames(tax_df)

final_df <- otu_long %>%
  left_join(tax_df, by = "ASV") %>%
  filter(Abundance > 0)

# 4. Write to Excel
write.xlsx(final_df, "../../microbiome/data/ASV_table_ostreobium_healthy_present.xlsx")
```

# SSU tree — build backbone

The following bash chunks document the HPC pipeline steps.
They are not executed on knit (`eval=FALSE`); adjust paths and
thread counts for your environment.

```{bash cluster-align, eval=FALSE}
# Prepare backbone sequences: cluster, align, trim
# Requires: vsearch, mafft, trimal

# 1. Sort by length
vsearch -sortbylength OST1611all.fa -output OST1611all.sorted.fa

# 2. Cluster at 99.5% identity
vsearch -cluster_smallmem OST1611all.sorted.fa -id 0.995 \
  -centroids OST1611all.clustered.fa -uc OST1611all.clustered.uc

# 3. Align
mafft --auto OST1611all.clustered.fa > OST1611all.aligned.fa

# 4. Trim
trimal -in OST1611all.aligned.fa -out OST1611all.aligned.trimal.fa \
  -gt 0.3 -st 0.001 -cons 30
```

```{bash modeltest, eval=FALSE}
# Select substitution model with ModelTest-NG
# Requires: modeltest conda environment

conda activate modeltest

modeltest-ng \
  -i OST1611all.aligned.trimal.fa \
  -d nt \
  -t ml \
  -p 16 \
  -T raxml \
  -o modeltest_OST.mtng
```

```{bash fasttree-check, eval=FALSE}
# Quick check with FastTree before running full RAxML
fasttreeMP -gtr -nt OST1611all.aligned.trimal.fa > OST1611all_fasttree.tre
```

```{bash raxml-backbone, eval=FALSE}
# Build backbone tree with RAxML
# Requires: raxml conda environment

conda activate raxml

raxmlHPC-PTHREADS \
  -T 16 \
  -m GTRGAMMAX \
  -p 31415 \
  -x 20398 \
  -d \
  -f a \
  -N 1000 \
  -n OST1611all.tre \
  -s OST1611all.aligned.trimal.fa
```

# EPA placement

## Extract Ostreobium sequences from full ASV FASTA

```{bash extract-seqs, eval=FALSE}
cd ../data

awk '
FNR==NR { arr[$0]; next }
/^>/ {
  found = ""
  match($0, /^>[^.]*/)
  if (substr($0, RSTART+1, RLENGTH-1) in arr) found = 1
}
found
' ostreobium_asvs_healthy.txt ASVs.fa > ASVs_extracted.fa

# Linearise (one sequence per line)
awk '/^>/ { printf("\n%s\n", $0); next } { printf("%s", $0) } END { printf("\n") }' \
  ASVs_extracted.fa > ASVs_extracted_oneline.fa

grep -c '>' ASVs_extracted_oneline.fa
```

## Align short reads to backbone HMM

```{bash epa-align, eval=FALSE}
# Requires: hmmer and trees conda environments

conda activate trees
cd EPA3

perl fasta2stockholm.pl OST1611all.aligned.fa > OST1611all.aligned.sto
hmmbuild OST1611all.hmm OST1611all.aligned.sto
hmmalign --dna --mapali OST1611all.aligned.fa OST1611all.hmm \
  ASVs_extracted_oneline.fa > epa.aligned.sto

# Convert to FASTA and clean up gap characters
perl stockholm2fasta.pl epa.aligned.sto > epa.aligned.fa
awk '/^>/ { print; next } { gsub("\\.", "-"); print }' epa.aligned.fa > cleaned_epa.aligned.fa
```

## ModelTest on EPA alignment

```{bash modeltest-epa, eval=FALSE}
conda activate modeltest

modeltest-ng \
  -i cleaned_epa.aligned.fa \
  -d nt \
  -t ml \
  -p 16 \
  -T raxml \
  -o modeltest_ost_EPA.mtng
```

## RAxML EPA placement

```{bash epa-placement, eval=FALSE}
raxmlHPC -T 4 -m GTRGAMMAIX -f v -G 0.2 \
  -n EPARUN.tre \
  -s cleaned_epa.aligned.fa \
  -t RAxML_bipartitions.OST1611all.tre

sed 's/QUERY___//g' RAxML_labelledTree.EPARUN.tre | sed 's/\[I[0-9]*\]//g' \
  > RAxML_placement_tree_ost_healthy_epa3.tre
```

# ASV counts per location / coral type

```{r asvs-by-location}
library(phyloseq)
library(dplyr)

# ps_ost_healthy_present should already be in memory from the extraction chunk above.
# If running standalone, reload ps_plas_V3_V4 and re-run the extraction chunk first.

locations <- c(
  "Central Pacific", "North East Pacific", "North West Atlantic",
  "Mediterranean Sea", "Red Sea", "Indian Ocean",
  "North West Pacific", "South West Pacific"
)

count_asvs_by_location <- function(ps, loc) {
  keep <- rownames(sample_data(ps))[sample_data(ps)$generic_location == loc]
  if (length(keep) == 0) return(0)
  ntaxa(prune_taxa(taxa_sums(prune_samples(keep, ps)) > 0, prune_samples(keep, ps)))
}

data.frame(
  generic_location = locations,
  ASV_count = sapply(locations, count_asvs_by_location, ps = ps_ost_healthy_present)
)
```

```{r asvs-by-coral-type}
groups <- c("complexa", "robusta", "octocoral")

count_asvs_by_group <- function(ps, grp) {
  keep <- rownames(sample_data(ps))[sample_data(ps)$complexa_robusta == grp]
  if (length(keep) == 0) return(0)
  ntaxa(prune_taxa(taxa_sums(prune_samples(keep, ps)) > 0, prune_samples(keep, ps)))
}

data.frame(
  complexa_robusta = groups,
  ASV_count = sapply(groups, count_asvs_by_group, ps = ps_ost_healthy_present)
)
```

```{r octocoral-ostreobium}
# Which octocoral species have Ostreobium?
ps_octo <- subset_samples(ps_ost_healthy_present, complexa_robusta == "octocoral")
ps_octo <- prune_taxa(taxa_sums(ps_octo) > 0, ps_octo)
length(taxa_names(ps_octo))
```
